summary: This work demonstrates fault-tolerant execution of two quantum algorithms—QAOA and HHL—using the $[[7,1,3]]$ Steane code on Quantinuum H2 and Helios trapped-ion processors, achieving near-break-even performance with encoded circuits outperforming unencoded ones for up to 8 logical qubits. The results include an improved logical $T$ gate with infidelity $2.6(4)\times10^{-3}$, identification of Steane-swap as the optimal QEC protocol, and key demonstrations that active error correction and repeat-until-success limits improve algorithm performance.
motivation: End-to-end fault-tolerant execution of complex quantum algorithms using only fault-tolerant components has remained unrealized despite progress on isolated error-correction primitives. Demonstrating this capability on current hardware is essential for validating the path toward scalable quantum computation.
method: We benchmarked individual fault-tolerant gadgets (specialized $|H\rangle$-state preparation, T-swap and T-bare $T$ gates, and three QEC variants) and systematically executed full QAOA circuits (5–12 logical qubits, up to 2132 physical two-qubit gates) and HHL circuits for the Poisson equation on trapped-ion systems, varying RUS limits and QEC cycle counts while using trasyn for Clifford+$T$ decomposition.
result: QAOA on LABS achieved $N\cdot p^*=12$ with 6–8 logical qubits performing comparably to unencoded execution; the 12-logical-qubit portfolio optimization circuit (97 physical qubits) outperformed random guessing; HHL fidelity reached $0.97\pm0.02$ with two QEC cycles inserted strategically, and increasing RUS limits reduced discard rates to nearly zero with minimal performance penalty.
